chapter_theme: What becomes of yogis and jnanis when they leave the body depends on how far they have come: the yogi passes through other worlds and returns to finish his yoga, while the faultless jnani rests in silent samadhi, becomes Siva and is not born again. To die to the three impurities while still living is the real death and the real attainment.
structure_note: The chapter climbs a ladder: the yogi's after-death course (1902 to 1904), the Siva-yogi who goes to a higher world and returns (1905), the jnani who does not return (1906), and then the jnani's state described from within: dying to the impurities (1907), acting by grace (1908) and pervading everything (1909).

1902.reading: A yogi who leaves the body in the waxing fortnight goes, it seems, by the gods' way into the sun's light, rests in the realm of the fathers and comes to what lies in the moon.
1902.nuance: வளர்பிறை (the waxing fortnight), தேவர் (gods), பானு (sun), பிதிர்பதம் (the fathers' station) and சசி (moon) recall the old teaching of two after-death paths, the gods' way through the sun and the fathers' way through the moon, and of death in the bright fortnight as auspicious. That is the traditional frame, not something the verse spells out; whether these are stages of one journey or alternatives is not clear from the Tamil.

1903.reading: A yogi who dies without reaching a samadhi equal to these goes to a world of refuge, then returns and, practising unbroken great yoga until what remains is spent, reaches the goal by relying on grace.
1903.nuance: The first line is corrupt, so 'without reaching samadhi' is a reconstruction. வியோகி may mean simply the yogi who has departed, or one fallen from yoga. The point that survives is that unfinished yoga is resumed in a later life rather than lost.

1904.reading: One who keeps in this way to the path open to people on earth advances through Siva-yoga by way of the bindu; if he is still imperfect before he becomes a full Siva-yogi, powers come to him and he takes on one body.
1904.nuance: விந்து (bindu), ஊனத்தோர் (the defective) and ஓர்காயம் (one body) are technical and unclear. Tradition takes the last line to mean that attainments short of the goal yield siddhis and a perfected or further body; it may equally mean one more embodiment. The verse places powers below full Siva-yoga.

1905.reading: When a Siva-yogi who has knowledge leaves a worn-out body, he reaches the world of austerity, then comes back and, through the knowledge of Siva-yoga, stands united; such people of merit are honoured by the worlds.
1905.nuance: தவலோகம் and புவலோகம் are taken as names of the upper worlds (tapoloka, bhuvarloka) in the Puranic scheme. 'Comes back' marks this as a step short of the jnani's case in the next verse.

1906.reading: When the faultless jnani who is also a true yogi leaves the body, he rests in a silent samadhi where the self is gone, becomes That, takes no other body, and as one freed without fault does not return.
1906.nuance: தானற ... தானவன் ஆகும் plays on self: the self ends and he becomes He. பரகாயம் usually names the siddhi of entering another's body; here the jnani needs no body at all. The verse sets this against the returns of 1903 to 1905.

1907.reading: If asked what the dead gain, it is to join pure consciousness; those who, still living in the world, have died to the three impurities become Siva and are the true siddhas.
1907.nuance: The verse turns on செத்தார் (the dead) used four times: bodily death in the first line, death to the three மலம் in the last two. சித்து may mean consciousness (chit) or Siva as consciousness, and the second line's syntax is loose. 'Dying while alive' is the plain point.

1908.reading: The strong one who has left birth behind protects, by Hara's grace, a lineage of grace, and for a jnani who asks even for sons the Lord gives form to what he wills.
1908.nuance: Most of this verse is obscure. கருவிட்டு is taken as leaving the womb, that is birth; அருட்குலம் as a lineage or community of grace, perhaps disciples; the last line as the Lord shaping things to the jnani's wish. Whether புதல்வர் means bodily sons or spiritual heirs cannot be settled from the Tamil.

1909.reading: For the Siva-jnani in whose heart grace dwells, Siva is everywhere and the Supreme is present everywhere; having died here, he stands everywhere as the Lord.
1909.nuance: The last line can be read with the jnani as subject (he becomes the all-pervading Lord) or with ஈசன் as subject (the Lord stands everywhere). The third line, on the sky that swallowed the world, is unclear.

links.note: The Siva-yogi of 1905 goes to a higher world and comes back; the faultless jnani of 1906 does not return. Together they rank the yogi below the jnani in what death brings.

Both make release a matter of not coming back: the Kural's மற்றீண்டு வாரா நெறி and Tirumular's மீளார். Tirumular adds the setting of a silent samadhi at death; the Kural says only that seeing the true thing here leads there.

1902 traces the yogi who dies in the waxing fortnight through the sun, the fathers' station and the moon. 1906 says the faultless jnani-yogi 'பரகாயம் சாராதே ... மீளார்', takes no other body and does not return. 1906 limits the celestial journeys of 1902 to those short of the jnani's state, which ends without any further station.

1903 says a yogi who dies before completing samadhi goes to a world of refuge and returns to take up unbroken yoga again. Kural 398 says learning gained in one birth 'எழுமையும் ஏமாப்புடைத்து', protects for seven. Both teach that inner gains outlast one life, the Kural for learning and the Tirumanthiram for yoga.

1904 says that before a yogi becomes a full Siva-yogi, siddhis come to him while he is still 'ஊனத்தோர்', lacking. 2619 separates 'ஒண்சித்தி முத்தியாம்', the bright attainment that is release, from the eight siddhis won by ending desire. Both rank the powers below release.

1909 says that for the Siva-jnani 'எங்கும் சிவமாய்', Siva is everywhere and the Supreme is present everywhere. 2722 says 'எங்கும் சிவமாய் இருத்தலால்', because Siva is everywhere, Chidambaram and the dance are everywhere too. They share the phrase; 2722 frees the sacred place, and 1909 frees the knower.

source_issues: 1903 line 1 is corrupt: 'சமாதிaக' contains a Latin 'a'; probably சமாதிக்கு or சமாதியைக்.
